titulo: Why Does Everyone Want to Be the DJ? A Topographic Flight
caption:
Why Does Everyone Want to Be the DJ? A Topographic Flight

The songwriter Dani Offline asks why so many people want to be the DJ. Making, she writes, has come to count for more than taking part. Without people who dance, she writes, the work has to get louder to be seen.

To us, taking part, sharing with others, is spiritual, because we are all connected. Try this: go where people dance, leave the phone in your pocket, and stay until you stop watching yourself. Where could you go dancing this week?

From "everyone wants to be a DJ, no one wants to dance" by Dani Offline, offline soul, 11 Sep 2025: https://danioffline.substack.com/p/everyone-wants-to-be-a-dj-no-one . Her words are retold as hers. The sentences about taking part and parties, the "try this" and the question are ours: our words, our view. Dani Offline did not make or endorse this video. Her essay and every NAOS strategy are on the NAOS page linked in our bio.

More strategies: link in bio.

descripcion:
Why do so many people want to be the DJ? The songwriter Dani Offline asks it in her essay "everyone wants to be a DJ, no one wants to dance". Making, she writes, has come to count for more than taking part.
In this topographic flight the canyon walls carry what people make to be seen. Then the camera bursts out over a wide basin that pulses like a dance floor.
To us, taking part, sharing with others, is spiritual, because we are all connected. Try this: go where people dance, leave the phone in your pocket, and stay until you stop watching yourself.

alt: Vertical topographic flight on near black. The camera races low down a canyon of warm white contour lines. The walls carry vermilion labels such as post, reel and review, and six fast cuts dive down side canyons. The walls grow taller and close in. In a short silence they end, and the camera bursts out over a wide basin of slow contours. The basin pulses ring to ring on the beat, like a wave through a crowd. Captions follow the voice, with a small "our words, our view" tag on our sentences. "Dani Offline" sits under her line about being most happy beyond any fixed identity or role. End card: where could you go dancing this week? and the credit.
